front: Are category design-load examples universal operating limits?
back: No. Use aircraft placard/POH. Lesson examples: normal ~4g, utility ~4.5g; type-specific.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Load limits</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>category</text><text x='54' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>examples</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>not universal</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>check POH</text></svg>

front: Why may trim be needed even when L=W and T=D?
back: Forces may balance while moments do not; CP/CG offsets and tail/downwash moments require balancing.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Forces vs moments</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>forces balance</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>moments remain</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>trim balances</text></svg>

front: What extra force component opposes climb along the flight path?
back: A rearward component of weight acts with drag, so more thrust/power is required.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Climb forces</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>climb path</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>weight</text><text x='159' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>component ←</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>drag ←</text></svg>

front: How does AoA in a steady climb compare with level flight at same speed/configuration?
back: Climb AoA is greater. Resolve forces relative to the flight path.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Climb and AoA</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>level</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>climb path ↑</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>AoA greater</text></svg>

front: What component of weight helps the aircraft in steady descent?
back: A component along the flight path aids motion down the path.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Descent forces</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>descent path ↓</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>weight</text><text x='159' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>component</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>aids motion</text></svg>

front: What do Vx and Vy mean?
back: Vx = best angle / greatest height per horizontal distance (obstacle clearance); Vy = best rate / height per time.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Climb speeds</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Vx</text><text x='54' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>best angle</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>obstacle</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Vy</text><text x='264' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>best rate</text></svg>

front: What are rate of climb and climb gradient?
back: ROC = vertical speed (e.g. ft/min); gradient = height gained per horizontal distance.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Climb measures</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>vertical</text><text x='54' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>ROC</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>horizontal</text><text x='159' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>distance</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>gradient</text></svg>

front: What standard obstacle height is used in the lesson take-off distance?
back: 50 ft / 15 m. Take-off distance includes ground roll plus distance to clear it.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Take-off distance</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>ground roll</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>50 ft / 15 m</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>clear obstacle</text></svg>

front: What factors affect take-off performance?
back: Weight, density/temperature, wind, runway surface/slope, power, flap setting and obstacles.
visual: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 150'><path d='M8 0 H312 Q320 0 320 8 V142 Q320 150 312 150 H8 Q0 150 0 142 V8 Q0 0 8 0 Z' fill='#fdf6e3'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='15' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>Take-off factors</text><line x1='98' y1='91' x2='108' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M108 86 L115 91 L108 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><line x1='203' y1='91' x2='213' y2='91' stroke='#526273' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M213 86 L220 91 L213 96 Z' fill='#526273'/><path d='M18 59 H90 Q98 59 98 67 V115 Q98 123 90 123 H18 Q10 123 10 115 V67 Q10 59 18 59 Z' fill='#dceeff' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='54' y='85' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>weight +</text><text x='54' y='97' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>density</text><path d='M123 59 H195 Q203 59 203 67 V115 Q203 123 195 123 H123 Q115 123 115 115 V67 Q115 59 123 59 Z' fill='#dff3df' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>wind + runway</text><path d='M228 59 H300 Q308 59 308 67 V115 Q308 123 300 123 H228 Q220 123 220 115 V67 Q220 59 228 59 Z' fill='#fff0d6' stroke='#263746' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='264' y='91' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='9.5' font-weight='bold' fill='#17212b'>power + flap</text></svg>

front: Define meteorological ceiling and the lesson’s service ceiling.
back: Met ceiling = lowest BKN/OVC layer; service ceiling here = altitude where climb rate falls to 100 ft/min under standard conditions.

front: In the simplified lesson technique, what controls descent path/rate and speed?
back: Power manages flight path/rate; pitch manages speed. Follow aircraft-specific technique.

front: What does PAPI/VASI indicate?
back: Visual path relative to the glide slope; it does not replace airspeed control.

front: What is a coordinated turn?
back: Banked lift provides the turn; balance lateral acceleration so there is no slip/skid. Keep the ball centred.

front: What determines bank required for a standard rate turn?
back: Primarily TAS: higher TAS needs more bank for the same turn rate. It does not depend on weight or wind.

front: Give turn radius at constant speed and bank.
back: r = V²/(g tanφ). At fixed bank, higher speed gives a wider turn.

front: Why is a propeller blade twisted from root to tip?
back: Tip rotational speed is higher; twist maintains a nearly constant effective AoA/load along the blade.

front: Define geometric and effective propeller pitch.
back: Geometric pitch = ideal advance per revolution; effective advance is less because of slip.

front: Which propeller pitch suits take-off and cruise?
back: Fine/low pitch suits take-off and low speed; coarse/high pitch suits cruise and high speed.

front: How does a fixed-pitch propeller behave?
back: RPM varies with throttle, airspeed and load; it is efficient near its design condition.

front: What does a constant-speed propeller governor maintain?
back: Selected RPM by changing blade pitch; it does **not** hold aircraft speed constant.

front: With increasing airspeed, how may a constant-speed propeller maintain RPM?
back: Blade pitch can increase to maintain selected RPM.

front: What do throttle and propeller controls primarily set?
back: Throttle/power control engine power; propeller control selects RPM. Respect engine/propeller limitations.

front: After engine failure, what does an unfeathered windmilling propeller do?
back: Produces drag, not useful thrust; feathering (if available) reduces drag.

front: What does propeller icing typically do?
back: Degrades blade aerofoil shape and typically reduces power and RPM.

front: Bank Q93: at idle descent, constant speed, prop lever moved aft—what happens?
back: Exam answer: pitch increases and sink rate decreases. Real operation follows the aircraft/engine POH.

front: Name four right-turning propeller secondary effects beyond the bank.
back: Slipstream, torque, gyroscopic precession and asymmetric blade thrust (P-factor). Direction/magnitude are aircraft-specific.
